chunks: Talḥah ibn Zayd narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"The sunnah (prophetic practice) has been established that the jizyah is not taken from the mentally impaired, nor from one overcome in his intellect."

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the established normative practice in Islamic law
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةُ: the poll tax levied under Islamic governance on certain non-Muslim subjects
key_terms.الْمَعْتُوهِ: a person with mental deficiency or severe impairment

ai.seo_question: From whom is jizyah not taken according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning jizyah, stating that it is not to be collected from those who are mentally impaired or whose intellect is overcome. It reflects a principle of legal consideration for diminished mental capacity in matters of financial obligation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1674 - Talha ibn Zayd narrated from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:
"The established practice (sunnah) is that jizya is not taken from the mentally ill or those whose intellect is impaired (maghlub ala 'aqlihi)."
